title: Expert Agents Team - 10 universal experts for review, opinion and consultation
description:
Create 11 universal expert agents that work like a real dev team. Same agent serves multiple contexts - review, opinion, direct consultation. Agent knows WHO it is, skill tells WHAT to do.

## Agents (agents/ directory)
1. architect - SOLID, patterns, system design
2. security-expert - OWASP, auth, crypto, secrets
3. backend-expert - API, logic, error handling, performance
4. database-expert - schema, migrations, queries, indexes, N+1
5. frontend-expert - React/Vue, TypeScript, a11y, CSS
6. devops-expert - Docker, CI/CD, nginx, shell scripts
7. qa-expert - test strategy, coverage, assertions, TDD
8. docs-expert - documentation sync, API docs, CLAUDE.md
9. compliance-expert - project rules, coding standards
10. git-historian - blame, history, past decisions
11. pragmatist - ROI vs effort, time-to-market, scope creep, business impact

## Skills to update/create
- lets-review: replace inline prompts with Task(subagent_type='lets:agent-name')
- lets-opinion: launch 3-5 relevant agents (architect + pragmatist always included)
- lets-ask (NEW): direct consultation with one expert

## Key decisions
- Agent file = expertise + personality. Skill prompt = task + context
- Auto model selection: haiku/sonnet/opus based on complexity
- Agents have Read/Grep/Glob + Bash where needed, no Edit/Write

## Design doc
docs/plans/2026-02-12-expert-agents-team-design.md

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
Expanded vision: instead of 10 narrow review agents, create 10 universal expert agents that work like a real dev team. Same agent serves multiple contexts:
- /lets-review: receives diff, returns issues
- /lets-opinion: receives decision, gives expert perspective
- Direct consultation: interactive dialog during development
- /feature-dev: helps plan architecture/implementation

Agent file defines expertise and personality. The skill/command determines the mode by passing appropriate context in the prompt. E.g. security-expert.md has broad security knowledge; /lets-review tells it 'review this diff', /lets-opinion tells it 'evaluate this decision'.

Need to brainstorm: exact expert roster, how skills pass context, how direct consultation works (new skill? command?).

comments.author: Dima Slep
comments.text:
## Progress 2026-02-12

### Done
- Brainstormed full concept: from 10 review agents to 10 universal experts
- Defined agent roster (10 experts with tools and expertise areas)
- Designed integration with lets-review, lets-opinion, lets-ask
- Designed auto model selection logic (haiku/sonnet/opus by complexity)
- Written and approved design document

### Key decisions
- Agent knows WHO, skill tells WHAT (separation of concerns)
- /lets-ask = 1 expert, /lets-opinion = 3-5 experts (clear boundary)
- No Edit/Write tools for agents (analyze only)
- Model auto-selected by context, --deep flag for upgrade

### Remaining
- Create 10 agent .md files in agents/
- Create /lets-ask skill
- Update /lets-review to use Task tool with agents
- Update /lets-opinion to launch agents in parallel
- Update CLAUDE.md
- Test each skill

### Artifacts
- docs/plans/2026-02-12-expert-agents-team-design.md
